findings.title: Unprotected setOwner() allows arbitrary contract ownership takeover
findings.description: A sensitive state-changing function is externally callable and the signature shows no modifier. It may be protected inside the body — triage will check.
findings.recommendation: Restrict with onlyOwner / role-based access control and emit events for each privileged action.

triage.reason: setOwner() is an external function without any authorization checks, allowing any user to take ownership of the contract.

findings.title: Authorization using tx.origin in emergencySweep allows phishing attacks
findings.description: tx.origin is the original signer, so any contract the victim interacts with can relay calls that pass this check (phishing-style attack).
findings.recommendation: Authorize with msg.sender (or a signature check) instead of tx.origin.

triage.reason: emergencySweep relies on tx.origin == owner for access control, exposing the function to phishing attacks via intermediate contract calls.

findings.title: Reentrancy vulnerability in withdrawAll allows draining vault funds
findings.description: An external call or token transfer happens before a later state write in the same function, with no nonReentrant guard. A malicious receiver or ERC-777/hook token can re-enter and act on stale state.
findings.recommendation: Apply checks-effects-interactions (update state before the call) and/or OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard.

triage.reason: withdrawAll() sends ETH balance via low-level call before updating balances[msg.sender] to 0, allowing reentrant balance withdrawal.

findings.title: Privileged owner is a single EOA
findings.evidence: owner() = 0xC0477B7C64fB76C4f5dFc083c9113D59556f5222 has no contract code on Base [Base Sepolia 0x70139e580853f6c54c976f027da3059f27e554ee]
findings.description: Functions guarded by the owner role are controlled by one private key. If it leaks, an attacker inherits every owner-only power (pausing, minting, fee changes, withdrawals — depending on the contract).
findings.recommendation: Transfer ownership to a multisig (Safe) and consider a timelock for sensitive actions.

findings.title: ERC-20 transfer/transferFrom return value ignored
findings.description: Some tokens (e.g. USDT-style) return false rather than reverting. Ignoring the result lets accounting drift from reality.

triage.reason: Line 40 transfers native ETH using address payable transfer, not an ERC-20 token transfer.

findings.title: Floating pragma
findings.description: Contracts should be deployed with the compiler version they were tested on.

triage.reason: Floating pragma ^0.8.20 is present; while locking exact compiler version is recommended, it is an informational best practice rather than an exploitable vulnerability.

limitations: Report AI stage produced by Google Gemini (provider: gemini, model: gemini-3.5-flash).
Exploit scenarios are reasoned from the code, not executed.
NightWatch is automated analysis, not a formal audit. Absence of findings is not a guarantee of safety.
